subject: Referring to data files from more than 1 app

messages.author: 0366928fd06f3534
messages.subject: Referring to data files from more than 1 app
parts:
I would like to have various data files, csv; rds SQLite which can be referred to by more than one app

I had thought of placing them all in one app 

locally in server.R of 'MyApp' I have a line equivalent to

df <- readRDS("../MyOtherApp/data.rds")

where the MyOtherApp holds the data

MyApp works fine

However, when I deploy MyApp and MyOtherApp to shinyapps.io/
I get the error message cannot open compressed file '../MyOtherApp/data.rds', probable reason 'No such file or directory'Error in gzfile(file, "rb") : cannot open the connection

TIA

messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Referring to data files from more than 1 app
parts:
Hi Andy, 

You can't share data across apps by including them in any one of the apps.  You would want to put them in a shared storage location like an S3, a database, or have them download the data from a common location. 

Here is the relevant paragraphs from the getting started guide:


1) Data written by an application to the local filesystem of an instance will be lost when you re-deploy the app. Additionally, the distributed nature of the ShinyApps.io platform means that instances may be shut down and re-created at any time for maintenance or to recover from server failures.

2) It is possible to have more than one instance of an application. This situation means that multiple instances of an application do not share a local filesystem. A file written to one instance will not be available to another instance.


We are considering whether we need to provide a shared data store of some kind, but we haven't gotten enough data to help us determine whether those added features would be ones that would be useful premium features.


-Tareef

messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Referring to data files from more than 1 app
parts:
Hi Andy,
We don't have storage limits yet.  The limit is really on the upload of the files you can send out on a per app basis.  The limit is currently set to 100MB.  Do you think that will work for you?  
We would love to learn more about the use cases to understand what else we need to be supporting in shinyapps.io for it to be a platform that works for you.

Best,
Tareef

It would be nice to access the same large SQLite db rather than deploy it with each app or have to do some preprocessing locally and deploy say a csv file with the data relevat to the blog entry
